full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. This civil petition for leave to Veal is directed against the judgment and order dated 6.8.2012, passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3221 of 2010 discharging the Rule and affirming the judgment and decree dated 10.08.2010 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Barguna, in Title Appeal No. 11 of 2008 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 15.8.2008, passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Pathargata, Barguna, in Title Suit No. 82 of 2003 decreeing the suit. 

 5. The learned Assistant Judge, Pathorgata, Barguna, upon hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 15.5.2008 holding that the plaintiff has been able to prove the case and that his absence was not unauthorized or illegal and rather he was on leave upon handing over the charge to defendant No.2. Challenging the same the defendant Nos.1 and 2 preferred Title Appeal No. 11 of 2008 before the learned District Judge, Barguna, which was ultimately heard by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Barguna, who vide judgment and decree dated 10.8.2010 allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court. Against the said judgment and decree dated 10.08.2010 the plaintiff moved the High court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 3221 of 2010. 

 6. The High Court Division, upon hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record, discharged the Rule by the impugned judgment and order dated 06.08.2012 affirming the judgment and decree of the court of appeal below dated 10.8.2010. Hence the plaintiff petitioner filed this civil petition for leave to appeal before this Court for redress. 

 8. Mr. Zainul Abedin, the learned Advocate-on-Record, appeared on behalf of the defendant respondent No.1 by filing caveat and submitted that the plaintiffs long absence from the office of the college was unauthorized in violation of the concerned Rules and as such the college authority upon observing all formalities dismissed him from service which the lower appellate Court as well as the High Court Division rightly appreciated and passed their respective judgments and as such no illegality has been committed by the appellate Court as well as by the High Court Division. But the trial Court on total non-appreciation of the materials on record decreed the suit which has been set aside by the lower appellate Court in accordance with law. He further submits that section 45 of the Ordinance of 1961 provides restriction of filing suit against any act done, order passed or proceeding taken by the President or the Government or the Board or by the Chairman or any other Officer of the Board or by any Committee under the Ordinance and as such the Managing Committee having been approved by the Board its action can-not be challenged in a suit. Hence, the plaintiffs suit is not maintainable under the law which the High Court Division rightly observed while passing the impugned judgment and order and as such the same is liable to be affirmed by this Division. 

 10. From the judgment of the trial Court it appears that in respect of the allegation of unauthorized absence, the trial Court observed that 'it is not believable that the plaintiff being founder principal and member secretary of the college would remain absent without proper permission from the college, for long. The Principal may go on leave upon taking permission of the authority'. On consideration of the evidence of D.W.2 found that he in his cross examination stated that 'during the period of leave when the plaintiffs wife was ill he handed over the charge to Md. Bari Azad (defendant No.2) and as such the plaintiff was not absent unauthorizedly and rather he was on leave and handed over charge to defendant No.2'. Accordingly, the trial Court decreed the suit. 

 Suspension being not the finality of the order the same cannot be challenged until it reaches the finality by approval and dismissal by the Board. And as such, institution of the suit seeking any relief, whatsoever, if results in an fruitless remedy the suit or the decree becomes ineffective which a Court does not generally grant. Thus, institution of the suit before the final dismissal order was passed is premature in law.
